name: Jules Drake
life: “I kept exact change in the hem of my coat for my first weekend job.” Monday often includes a stop at the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms, where Jules prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I still have her loose change in a jar. It buys exactly one sandwich at the old price.
appearance: Jules is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and a narrow face with an expressive upper lip. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Jules starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak when listening.
personality: Jules has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Jules can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To buy one sandwich at the remembered price.
family: Joel Sun is Jules’s older relative by marriage. Jules asks before bringing somebody along. Joel can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The last light at the harbor*, Joel says, “I lived on the smallest boat after my divorce and still count its light even though another family sleeps there.”
connections: Fiona Mann. The remaining change and the wrapper give the anniversary order a price and a proper finish.

reactions.situation: A relative hates the ingredient everyone remembers
reactions.response: Jules lets the relative choose a different sandwich without defending the menu.
